html:
The Mississauga are an Anishinaabe people, close kin of the Ojibwe, whose name refers to the mouth of the Mississagi River on the north shore of Lake Huron. The map gives them a wide area of southern Ontario in 1492, though in that period the land near Lake Ontario was held mainly by Huron and other Iroquoian peoples.

After the Haudenosaunee destroyed the Huron in the Beaver Wars of the mid 1600s, the Anishinaabe pushed back south. By about 1700 the Mississauga had settled on the north shore of Lake Ontario.

From the 1780s they sold most of this land to the British, including the site of Toronto in the Toronto Purchase of 1787. The Mississaugas of the Credit, led in the 1800s by the Methodist preacher Peter Jones, now live near Hagersville, and in 2010 Canada paid them for the unfair Toronto deal. The city of Mississauga takes their name.
